label: Monado MGC
title: Monado MGC (HP Reverb G2)
intro: The MGC calibration recordings of the Monado SLAM Datasets, made with an HP Reverb G2 headset: its 4 tracking cameras, recorded as three pairs (cam0 + cam1, cam0 + cam2, cam1 + cam3), and its IMU.

image.alt: HP Reverb G2 headset, front view
image.credit: Photo: HP, Reverb G2 press release

reading: Three camera pairs. Each recording shows the board to one pair of cameras. T5 and T12 are pair 01 (cam0 + cam1) and belong to the leaderboard batch. Pairs 02 (cam0 + cam2) and 13 (cam1 + cam3) are from separate runs of 2026-11-27 and have no row on the Leaderboard. A camera that is in two pairs has one set of values per pair.
Kalibr on pairs 02 and 13. We ran Kalibr camera + IMU as on pair 01 and did not tune it. It did not give a usable solve on any of the 8 recordings, so all its values there are shown grey.

families.title: cam0 + cam1 + IMU
families.read_first: Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from an MVIS export; its td and lever are solved given them.
notes: MVIS uses the local gravity of Córdoba (9.7931 m/s², 0.17 % below 9.81), so its Da sits about 0.17 % lower than with 9.81; Kalibr and Basalt use a fixed standard gravity.

the camera + IMU twin of T5 (same pair, same 4 sessions). Both tools start from the camera calibration of the same round: MVIS from T5 camera-only (refined in cam-IMU), Kalibr from the MVIS T12 export (fixed).
the kb4 rows, seeded from Basalt's T5 round.

families.title: cam0 + cam2 stereo
families.read_first: Kalibr and Basalt calibrate both cameras and their baseline from the images alone, on the 4 camcalib02 recordings. MVIS calibrates each camera alone.
notes: Every tool ran on the same 4 recordings, each with its own camera model: MVIS equidistant, Kalibr pinhole-equi and Basalt kb4, the same polynomial.
MVIS calibrates each camera of this pair alone (its joint camera-only solve of the pair fails), so it has no baseline here; Kalibr and Basalt solve the pair jointly.
families.no_mvis: solves each camera of this pair alone here, so it has no baseline. Kalibr and Basalt solve the pair together.

families.title: cam0 + cam2 + IMU
families.read_first: MVIS starts from its per-camera results of the same round and refines the intrinsics. Kalibr's intrinsics and baselines are inputs from an MVIS export; its td, lever and IMU intrinsics are solved given them.

poor.text: Its IMU scales are far from 1 on every recording: gyro scale 1.2 to 12, accelerometer scale z 1.2 to 7860.

notes: Every tool ran on the same 4 recordings, each with its own camera model: MVIS equidistant, Kalibr pinhole-equi and Basalt kb4, the same polynomial.
MVIS starts from its per-camera camera-only results of the same round and refines the intrinsics; Kalibr's cameras are fixed at the MVIS result; no MVIS default-IMU-model run.
kb4, seeded from Basalt's MGC02-cam round.
